Synthesis and characterization of dense and porous cellulose films
top_cited_works.abstract: Abstract Whereas cellulose‐derived polymers are routinely used as membrane materials, the cellulose polymer itself is not directly used to synthesize dense/porous films for membrane applications. Recently, N‐methylmorpholine N‐oxide (NMMO) and dimethylacetamide (DMAc)/lithium chloride (LiCl) have been successfully employed for dissolving unmodified cellulose. This provides a strong rationale for reexamining the possibility of cellulose membrane fabrication using these solvents. By judiciously selecting solvents, casting conditions, and solvent exchange steps, we successfully synthesized dense/asymmetric‐porous cellulose films. The pore size and porosity of the porous films decreased systematically with increasing cellulose concentration. SEM analysis of the cross sections revealed an asymmetric skinned structure with monotonically increasing pore size away from the skin. The measured pore diameters were in the range 1.8–4.8 μm. Mechanical testing indicated that the dense films possessed tensile properties comparable to those of cellulose acetate (CA) films. recent_works.title: Design of Thermally Activated Foldable Bio-inspired Wing for Micro Air Vehicles
recent_works.abstract: Micro Air Vehicles (MAVs) are critical for surveillance and search-and-rescue, yet tradi tional designs often struggle with weight penalties and mechanical complexity. Inspired by the segmented architecture in the Potter Wasp (Antodynerus punctatipennis), the actuation kinematics in this paper adopt the transverse Z-folding mechanism of Coleoptera (beetles) to maximize stowage efficiency. Utilizing composite segments connected by Veriflex shape memory polymer (SMP) hinges, the design aims to achieve a compact structure that maintains flight-ready rigidity. Unlike traditional mechanisms that rely on heavy servos, this design utilizes composite panels actuated by Veriflex Shape Memory Polymer (SMP) hinges to achieve a 56% reduction in planform area. Dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) and isothermal tensile tests were performed for the viscoelastic stress relaxation modeling using time-temperature superposition. Finite element analysis demonstrates a shape fixity of 96.9%, confirming the material’s ability to lock the stowed configuration without auxiliary latches. recent_works.title: Probing Shape Recovery in Thin-Ply Composites With Shape Memory Effect
recent_works.abstract: Shape recovery in plain-weave carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) thin-ply composites is studied with a new SMP-epoxy polymer matrix. Static tensile and viscoelastic relaxation experiments were performed on the proposed SMP-epoxy test coupons to obtain long-term relaxation and elastic properties. Using experimental inputs, the time-dependent behavior of plain-weave CFRP laminates modeled using the laminate homogenization method is analyzed at the coupon scale. Storage and deployment of CFRP structures are simulated using the Column Bending Test (CBT). The effect of shape-memory polymer (SMP) on bending-relaxation in CFRP laminated was investigated through CBT simulation. The bending moment and curvature in CFRP coupons are analyzed as a precursor to propose SMP-epoxy polymer in CFRP for deployable space structures.

recent_works.title: Shear Lag in High-Throughput Testing of Thin-Ply Composites
recent_works.abstract: High throughput testing methods have significant potential to reduce experimental efforts in determining mechanical, time-dependent, and multifunctional properties with reduced time and cost. Imposing a known stress gradient on the gauge length of the test coupon is one of the most recent test methodologies. The stress gradient based high throughput testing scheme is well proven for low density polymers and the off-axis unidirectional composite laminates. However, the shear lag due to interfacial interaction between the loaded and the unloaded fibers in 0°UD composite laminates is still a challenge, which limits the scope of high throughput testing. Based on our previous experimental learnings, this paper is an analytical and computational attempt to circumvent the shear lag that varies from the boundary to the middle region of geometrically tailored test specimen. The study shows that the shear lag in trapezoidal specimen with an imposed stress gradient could be restricted to the boundary only, thereby holding a uniaxial state of stress in the middle zone for high throughput data extraction.

Flexible DIC System for Wind Tunnel Testing of Lightweight Structures
recent_works.abstract: We propose an adjustable digital image correlation (DIC) system for the wind tunnel testing of small and large-scale aerospace and civil structures. A novel mounting rig with azimuth and pitch rotation fixtures was designed and developed for the DIC setup that can be installed from outside of the wind tunnel test section. The independent mounting rig makes the DIC system adjustable as per the shape and size of the test structure, which can reduce the installation and calibration efforts in wind tunnel testing. Telecentric lenses optimize the far-field optics of the DIC system. It allows the user to implement a rigorous calibration procedure to study magnification effects. We calibrated the DIC system at various fields of view and depths of field to ensure its suitability for wind tunnel experiments in which accuracy is a prime concern. The DIC measurements can be verified with the Euler transformation algorithm with a suitable combination of azimuth, pitch, and camera optical parameters.
